external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: Customers browse and order socks through the mobile app and receive faxed confirmations.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

external_entities.name: Marketing
external_entities.description: The marketing team maintains the catalogue spreadsheet.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile app lets customers browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The web API stores customer information, receives orders, hands orders to SIMS, and accepts catalogue changes from spreadsheet macros.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: SIMS is the stock and inventory system that processes orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The fax gateway dials the number stored against an order and faxes a customer confirmation.
processes.source_excerpt: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The user database contains customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me ... whether the user database ... [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: The flat file contains delivery addresses and nothing else.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me ... whether ... the flat file [is] encrypted.

data_stores.name: catalogue spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The catalogue spreadsheet contains the marketing catalogue and its macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy. It is stored on a marketing laptop in the office.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: app talks to API
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: hand order over
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write delivery address
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
data_flows.data_description: dispatch note containing the customer's name and address

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it.
data_flows.notes: Nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: confirmation with the customer's name and address

data_flows.name: maintain catalogue
data_flows.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

data_flows.name: change prices and copy
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office is the stated location of the marketing laptop holding the catalogue spreadsheet.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes it as a mobile app rather than a website or web application.
The source describes SIMS as a stock and inventory system and does not describe a web interface.

assumptions.assumption: The fax gateway presents a non-web interface.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a fax gateway rather than a web application.
It contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.

assumptions.assumption: The office is a network trust boundary.
assumptions.basis: The source places the marketing laptop in the office, which identifies a distinct network location.
